rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (kp 2.0, kd 0.1, ki 0.3, base_speed 1.0, search_right, sensor_size 0.012) is the best raced design at 75.779. Iteration 8 raised kd to 0.2 and scored 69.031, with lower progress on all three tracks (oval 0.29 to 0.27, s-bend 0.15 to 0.137, slalom 0.11 to 0.089) and higher oval oscillation (0.16 to 0.17). Raising kd did not reduce max_error (about 0.062 m on every track), so damping is not the limiter. Iterations 6 (kp 1.6) and 7 (sensor_size 0.016) both lost progress, so kp 2.0 and sensor_size 0.012 stay.

Change: kd returns to 0.1. base_speed goes from 1.0 to 1.1. Everything else is the iteration 5 design: kp 2.0, ki 0.3, search_right, sensor weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], sensor_size 0.012, and sensor x positions of -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04 at y 0.05. Iterations 3 and 4 showed that speed moves progress between the oval and the bend tracks, so this is a small test of whether bend progress rises without losing the oval.

Expected result: slalom and s-bend progress above iteration 5 while the oval holds near 0.29. Hypothesis: the remaining failure is a slow drift to one edge that speed alters, not a damping or sensing problem. Fallback: if oval progress falls or line_loss_events rises, return base_speed to 1.0 and accept iteration 5 as the best gain set.

Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and whether the loss point moves along the course.
